subject: Post-call recap: Dedicated capacity options & next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Laura Reynolds <laura@pulsemed.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Dedicated capacity options & next steps

Hi Laura —

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our conversation and the next steps we discussed so your team has a single reference: 

Key pain points you shared:
- Unpredictable latency at peak times for clinical batch scoring jobs (spikes of 3–7s/token impacting UX).
- Strict data isolation and audit requirements for patient PII (needs VPC/private endpoints + customer-managed keys).
- Need predictable throughput for nightly processing windows and predictable monthly spend for forecasting.

Goals we aligned on:
- Reserved dedicated GPU capacity (isolation) rather than shared hosted endpoints.
- SLA targets: 99.9% availability and 95th-percentile token latency below 150ms for interactive workloads; higher latency ok for batch jobs if throughput guarantees met.
- Autoscaling/burst for traffic spikes with controlled burst capacity to avoid cold-starts.
- Integrations: VPC peering, KMS key management, and audit log export to your SIEM.

Recommended initial configuration (engineering / pricing sketch):
- 4x A100-equivalent GPU nodes reserved (baseline) + ability to burst +2 nodes for peak windows.
- Private control plane with VPC peering and private endpoints to satisfy isolation requirements.
- KV/prefix caching enabled for interactive flows; batch workers routed to dedicated batch queue.
- SOC2/Pen-test evidence & KMS integration checklist (we will attach evidence / orchestration doc).

Next steps (owners & timeline):
1) Ben (me) — send procurement-ready quote and capacity diagram by EOD tomorrow. (Attachment: quote PDF + diagram)
2) Dylan — schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive next week to review network/KMS and rollout plan.
3) PulseMed procurement — loop in legal /billing to review quote and preferred contracting cadence.
4) Marissa — prep SOW stub and proposed rollout timeline for the first 90 days.

Questions / clarifications: if the baseline should be 6 reserved GPUs instead of 4 based on your throughput targets, let us know and we can adjust the quote.

Attaching: pulsemed_dedicated_capacity_quote_v2.pdf, capacity_diagram.png

Thanks again — excited to get this moving.

Best,
Ben Carter

Contract / commercial notes for procurement:

- Payment terms: Net 30 by default; we can discuss Net 45 for enterprises.

Operational rollout (proposed 90-day plan):

Week 2-4: Network setup (VPC peering, private endpoints), KMS onboarding
Week 4-6: Provision reserved GPU pool + test workloads (staging)
Week 6-12: Pilot, monitoring tuning, and cutover
